The Prophet asks Allah's mercy on Lot, who wanted powerful support, and says that after a stay in prison as long as Joseph's he would have accepted release.
Told of the story spread about her, Aisha faints and wakes with fever, likening her case to Jacob's with his sons, until verses come and she thanks only Allah.
Aisha explains verse 12.110: the apostles despaired of their disbelieving nations and feared even their followers wavered, never doubting their Lord, until Allah's help came.
Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, is the honourable son of honourable fathers.
Job, bathing, gathered falling gold locusts, and when his Lord asked whether He had not made him rich enough, said he could never do without His blessing.
Returning to Khadija with a pounding heart, the Prophet is taken to Waraqa, a Christian reader of the Gospels, who says it was the angel Allah sent to Moses.
The Prophet says none should call him better than Jonah, and recounts his Night Journey: Aaron in the fifth heaven, Moses and Jesus described, and milk chosen over wine.
Finding Medina's Jews fasting Ashura for the day Allah saved Moses and drowned Pharaoh's folk, the Prophet says he is closer to Moses, fasts it and orders Muslims to fast.
When people fall unconscious on Resurrection Day, the Prophet, first to recover, will see Moses holding a pillar of the Throne, perhaps spared for his swoon at the Tur.
Were it not for the Children of Israel meat would not decay, and were it not for Eve no woman would betray her husband.
Moses, saying none is more learned, seeks Al-Khadir where the fish is lost but cannot stay patient as Khadir holes a boat, kills a boy and mends a wall.
Bani Israel change 'Repentance' at the gate; Moses, said to hide a defect, is cleared when a stone runs off with his clothes, and he bore worse harm patiently.
Picking Arak fruit, the Prophet says the black ones are best, and when asked if he had been a shepherd, says every prophet was one.
Moses slaps the Angel of Death, is offered a year for each hair under his hand on an ox, but chooses death now near the Sacred Land.
The Prophet forbids preferring him over Moses, whom he will see holding Allah's Throne at the Resurrection; Adam answers Moses' blame with his written fate; Moses' followers fill a horizon.
Of women only Asia, Pharaoh's wife, and Mary, daughter of Imran, reached perfection, and Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other meals.
None should say the Prophet is better than Jonah bin Matta; angered when an Ansari slapped a Jew over Moses, he forbade ranking Allah's prophets above one another.
Reciting the Psalms was made easy for David, who ate only from his own labour; his fasting on alternate days and his night prayer are the most beloved to Allah.
Asked about prostrating at Surat Sad, Ibn Abbas cites the verse telling the Prophet to follow David, Solomon and earlier prophets; it is not compulsory, though the Prophet prostrated.
The Prophet freed a demon he caught, recalling Solomon's prayer for a unique kingdom; Solomon, not saying 'If Allah will' over seventy women, had only a half child born.
Al-Masjid al-Haram was the first mosque built and Al-Aqsa the next, forty years apart, and wherever prayer time comes the whole earth is a place of prayer.
The Prophet likens himself and people to a man whose fire draws moths, and tells how Solomon gave a child two women disputed to the younger, reversing David.
When companions feared the verse on mixing belief with wrong, the Prophet explained that wrong as joining others in worship with Allah, citing Luqman's advice to his son.
On the night of his Ascension the Prophet met John and Jesus, cousins, in the second heaven, and they welcomed him as a pious brother and pious prophet.
Satan touches every newborn but Mary and her son; Mary is named with Khadija as best of women and with Asia as perfect; Quraish women are best of camel-riding women.
Whoever testifies that none but Allah may be worshipped, that Muhammad and Jesus are His slaves and apostles, Jesus His Word and spirit, and Paradise and Hell true, enters Paradise.
Three spoke in the cradle: Jesus, a baby who cleared the Israelite Juraij of a false charge, and an infant who preferred a falsely accused slave girl to a tyrant.
The Prophet describes Moses, Jesus and Abraham as seen on the night of his Ascension, when he chose milk over wine and was told he had taken the right path.
In a dream at the Ka'bah the Prophet saw Jesus circling it, brown with lank dripping hair, and behind him the Dajjal, curly-haired and blind in the right eye.
The Prophet is nearest to Jesus, prophets sharing one religion; Jesus believed a thief's oath; do not overpraise the Prophet as Christians did Jesus; believers in both get double reward.
People will be resurrected barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, Abraham clothed first; some companions will be taken aside as renegades, and the Prophet will answer in the words of Jesus.
The son of Mary will descend as a just ruler, breaking the cross, killing pigs and ending the jizya, when wealth is so plentiful that nobody accepts it.
The Dajjal's fire will be cool water; among earlier people Allah forgave a man who eased his debtors and another who had his body burnt out of fear of Him.
On his deathbed the Prophet invoked Allah's curse on the Jews and Christians for building places of worship at their prophets' graves, warning Muslims against doing so.
Prophets ruled the Israelites one after another, but after the Prophet will come caliphs: obey the first given the pledge and give them their rights, for Allah will question them.
Muslims will follow Jews' and Christians' ways; the adhan and a prayer posture differ from theirs; a parable gives Muslims double wages; Jews are cursed for selling forbidden fat.
Convey the Prophet's teaching even one sentence; telling stories of the Children of Israel is no sin; whoever deliberately lies about the Prophet takes his place in the Fire.
The Jews and Christians do not dye their grey hair, so Muslims are told to do the opposite.
Among earlier peoples a suicide was denied Paradise, three Israelites were tested with health and wealth, three trapped in a cave were freed by sincere deeds, and a baby spoke.
An Israelite prostitute took off her shoe to water a dog dying of thirst, and Allah forgave her for it.
